Style BookiOS app case study
UI/UX design · iOS

Dressed to fit.

A fashion shopping app for iOS where you can buy from popular brands or get a suit tailored to your measurements, with a home visit from a tailor.

iOS app24 screensUI/UX designiPhone 17 Pro
✂Made-to-measure
⌂Home tailor visit
✓Track your order

Shop, customize and track clothing with ease, using an app built for fit, choice and trust: from popular brands to a suit cut to your own measurements.

Designed to give shoppers one clear path from first browse to a tailor at the door, so they always know what happens next.

01 · Brand identity

The Style Book logo.

The logo is built from a tailor’s three tools: a needle, a button and a measuring tape. It comes in two forms: the SB monogram for the app icon, and the full wordmark for the brand name.

03 · Sign in

Phone number, then four digits.

Phone-number login with inline validation and a 4-digit OTP step, kept short so people reach the clothes faster.

  • AInline validation before you tap continue
  • BFour digits, not six: fewer taps to the clothes
OTP

07 · Profile

Everything in one place.

08 · Errors and empty states

Every dead end has a next step.

Clear messages and one action for each dead end: missing pages, lost connection, server errors, an empty cart, failed payments, and a forced update.

09 · Design system

Deep plum, one hot orange.

A deep plum base with a single hot orange for actions gives a premium-tailoring feel, with one clear call to action per screen.

Persimmon#FF5C35 · action
Plum#341F26 · base
Deep plum#1E1115 · stage
Cream#FBF8F6 · surface
Lilac#AFB0FF · accent

Headline: Unbounded

Unbounded

Wide, heavy display type adds fashion-editorial character. Used for headlines, numerals and short labels.

Body: Albert Sans

Albert Sans

A clean sans keeps copy, buttons and form fields readable at any size.

One confident accent

Persimmon is the only loud colour. It marks the single most important action on a screen, never more than one per view.

Tag-card is the module

A punched hole and a stitched inset border make a garment tag, not a generic panel: the system’s signature container.

FIT

Made to fit, down to the stitch.
